Messages.Author: edminister
Messages.Body: Can I Govern down an Imbued and modify the action with Ghouled?

Messages.Author: Timo
Messages.Body:
An imbued is not a younger vampire.

therefore you can't play govern superior on it.

And even if you could (with another sort of card yet to be created) it would not be a "recruit" action and so you couldn't modify it with ghouled.

Messages.Author: Brum
Messages.Body:
Please copy+paste the text of the cards you ask questions about.

Like this:

Name: Govern the Unaligned
Cardtype: Action
Cost: 1 blood
Discipline: Dominate
[dom]  Bleed with +2 bleed.
[DOM] +1 stealth action. Move 3 blood from the bank to a younger vampire in your uncontrolled region.

Thank you.

PS: Govern says "..to a younger vampire...". Imbued are not vampires. They are mortal allies.
So, no.

Messages.Author: edminister
Messages.Body:
Copying and pasting the text of cards is a lot of work when you want a simple and quick answer, I am asking a question not writing a book. I get it for obscure cards and whatnot but this was more a concept question. You will note that an answer was given before you insisted that descriptions be listed. From now on I will ask in other forums as this one seems to be... uptight.

An action taken to move pool onto an uncontrolled minion in the crypt is evidently NOT a recruitment action despite the fact that by description that is exactly what you are doing with cards like Govern. If this is a living game and we expect to see other expansions in the future that do not focus primarily on vampires this might need to be clarified.

As it stands, the Nights of Reckoning set is the biggest rules addendum so far and for what? A handful of minions that are all in the same group with what appears to be no future releases for it, admit it as a mistake and ban the damned things now and move on with lessons learned or get creative and build on it for better or worse. I was simply asking to see if there was some way to integrate them into what is already a solid game mechanic a little better than bringing a couple out, screwing about with convictions for 20 minutes while the rest of the table pulls up rules addendums on their phones, and then dropping gehenna events that don't affect them because of their semi-ally status. It's boring and the only other practical use for them other than generating table hate is to roll with weapons, targets, and disciplineless actions and combat cards which simply cannot stand in the face of real combat decks.

Messages.Author: ReverendRevolver
Messages.Body:
If you want quirky modified imbued, putrescent servitude makes them able to play potence(not just potence strike like craptastic ghouled) and i think it gives an extra life.......

Anyway, its a really shitty card. Thats why they mentioned copy n paste, it is kinda obscure, and it does help since most people dont remember what ghouled says.
Some cards are better than you assume when first reading it. Ghouled is worse than you assume when first reading it...

And recruit is, as stated in the rules, an action to put an ally into play. Thus, with cards like the summoning, you could ghouled an ally not in your hand. But since even a govern to an imbued is never putting them into play, or described as recruiting, its not a recruit action.

Messages.Author: Boris The Blade
Messages.Body:
> Brum wrote:
> PS: Govern says "..to a younger vampire...". Imbued are not vampires. They are mortal allies.
> So, no.
>
It is not so simple. There are cards that are written "vampires" but that can target Imbued, and the whole rulings section in the Imbued rules is dedicated to it. The rule of thumb is: if you can see what you are targeting, then vampire means vampire. If you cannot, then vampire means crypt card.

Govern the Unaligned targets cards in your uncontrolled region, and you can look at those at any time, so vampire really means vampire in that case, and it cannot target an Imbued.

EDIT: it seems that card texts online have been updated to replace all the wrong "vampire" with "uncontrolled minion" or something similar, but many of those cards have never been reprinted.

Messages.Author: self biased
Messages.Body:
> edminister wrote:
> An action taken to move pool onto an uncontrolled minion in the crypt is evidently NOT a recruitment action despite the fact that by description that is exactly what you are doing with cards like Govern. If this is a living game and we expect to see other expansions in the future that do not focus primarily on vampires this might need to be clarified.
>
i mean, i get that's largely the end result, but an action that puts counters on cards in your crypt is just that: an action that puts counters on cards in your crypt. A recruit action is pretty specific in its scope:

> the wrote:
> 6.1.5. Recruit Ally (+1 stealth)
>
> Allies are action cards that become minions in their own right, capable of acting and blocking independently of the minion that recruits them. The recruit ally action has a default +1 stealth.
>
> To recruit an ally from your hand, play the card and tap the acting minion. If the action is successful, the ally is placed in your uncontrolled region, even though it is controlled, to indicate that it cannot act this turn (and the cost, if any, is paid). If the action is unsuccessful, the card is burned (see Resolve the Action, sec. 6.2.3). Only one ally card can be recruited per action. Note that allies brought into play by other means are able to act on the same turn, by default.
>
> At the end of the turn, any allies that were placed in your uncontrolled region (to indicate that they cannot act) are moved to your ready region.
> When an ally is brought into play (by any means), he receives blood counters from the blood bank to represent his life (listed on the ally's card). When an ally loses his last life counter, he is burned. If recruiting the ally requires a Discipline and the ally is put into play by some means other than recruiting, use the normal version of the ally, if it is different than the superior.
>

Our forums, not unlike the entire internet, has useful information mixed with opinions mixed with good ideas mixed with trolling.

Messages.Author: Pascal Bertrand
Messages.Body:
> edminister wrote:
> Can I Govern down an Imbued and modify the action with Ghouled?
>
Correct answer from Brum in page 1. You can't Govern down to an Imbued.

Here's an extract of the Nights of Reckoning Rules addendum:
Nights of Reckoning page  wrote:
>
> In earlier sets, card effects that deal with crypt cards have generally assumed that crypt cards were all vampires. Now that this is no longer true, some questions arise.
>
> In general, if you (the Methuselah playing the card or activating the effect) can look at the crypt card (e.g., because it is in your uncontrolled region or in any ash heap or in play, or if you're "searching" your crypt), then the target crypt card must match the parameters given by the effect. This usually means that imbued cannot be targets of these effects.
>
> If you target a crypt card "blind" (either an unseen card from the crypt or an unseen card in some other Methuselah's uncontrolled region), then work with whatever you find. If the effect only checks/compares the card's "capacity", then treat the imbued's cost (starting life) as its capacity for that comparision.
>
